WITH RECURSIVE houston_employee_base AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        e.Ssn,
        e.Fname,
        e.Lname,
        e.Salary,
        e.Super_ssn
    FROM employee e
    INNER JOIN works_on w ON e.Ssn = w.Essn
    INNER JOIN project p ON w.Pno = p.Pnumber
    WHERE p.Plocation = 'Houston'
),
supervisory_hierarchy AS (
    SELECT 
        Ssn,
        Fname,
        Lname,
        Salary,
        Super_ssn,
        0 AS tier_level,
        Ssn AS origin_emp_id
    FROM houston_employee_base
    
    UNION ALL
    
    SELECT 
        e.Ssn,
        e.Fname,
        e.Lname,
        e.Salary,
        e.Super_ssn,
        sh.tier_level + 1,
        sh.origin_emp_id
    FROM supervisory_hierarchy sh
    INNER JOIN employee e ON sh.Super_ssn = e.Ssn
    WHERE sh.Super_ssn IS NOT NULL
),
ranked_hierarchies AS (
    SELECT 
        sh.origin_emp_id,
        sh.Fname,
        sh.Lname,
        sh.tier_level,
        sh.Salary,
        COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY sh.origin_emp_id ORDER BY sh.tier_level ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cum_salary_rank
    FROM supervisory_hierarchy sh
    WHERE sh.origin_emp_id IN (SELECT Ssn FROM houston_employee_base)
)
SELECT 
    rh.Fname || ' ' || rh.Lname AS EmployeeName,
    rh.tier_level AS HierarchyLevel,
    SUM(rh2.Salary) AS CumulativeSalary
FROM ranked_hierarchies rh
INNER JOIN supervisory_hierarchy rh2 
    ON rh.origin_emp_id = rh2.origin_emp_id 
    AND rh2.tier_level <= rh.tier_level
GROUP BY rh.origin_emp_id, rh.tier_level
ORDER BY rh.origin_emp_id, rh.tier_level;

JOIN dept_locations dl ON e.Dno = dl.Dnumber

    SELECT d.Sex
    FROM dependent d
    JOIN works_on w ON d.Essn = w.Essn
    WHERE w.Hours > 20

    ROUND(COUNT(*) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM filtered_dependents), 2) AS percentage
FROM filtered_dependents
